topics: MLE parameter derivation for Gaussian mean and variance

body.en: Data in AI is modeled using probability distributions. Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) is the statistical method used to find the model parameters that make the observed training data most probable.

Given independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations \( X = \{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_N\} \) from a distribution parameterized by \( \theta \):
1. Likelihood: \( L(\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^N p(x_i | \theta) \).
2. Log-Likelihood: \( \ell(\theta) = \ln L(\theta) = \sum_{i=1}^N \ln p(x_i | \theta) \). Taking the logarithm converts products into sums without shifting the maximizing argument.
3. MLE Estimator: \( \hat{\theta}_{\text{MLE}} = \arg\max_\theta \ell(\theta) \), solved by setting \( \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \theta} = 0 \).

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Mathematics for Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).
body.ar: برهان النسب المتتالية والسرعة المتوسطة التوافقية: عند زيادة مقدار بنسبة \(p\%\) ثم خفضه بنسبة \(p\%\) يكون الناتج \(Q_0(1 - (p/100)^2) < Q_0\)، والسرعة المتوسطة لرحلتين متساويتين في المسافة هي الوسط التوافقي \(\frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example 5.A — Deriving the MLE of a Bernoulli Parameter

body.en:
Let \( x_1, x_2, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\} \) be \( N \) binary outcomes from a coin toss with unknown bias \( p \). Deriving the MLE estimator for \( p \).

Solution:
The probability of single outcome is \( P(x_i) = p^{x_i}(1-p)^{1-x_i} \).
The likelihood for \( N \) i.i.d. observations is:
\[ L(p) = \prod_{i=1}^N p^{x_i}(1-p)^{1-x_i} = p^{\sum x_i} (1-p)^{N - \sum x_i} \]
Let \( k = \sum_{i=1}^N x_i \) be the total number of successes.
Log-likelihood:
\[ \ell(p) = \ln L(p) = k \ln p + (N - k) \ln(1 - p) \]
Differentiate with respect to \( p \) and set to 0:
\[ \frac{d\ell}{dp} = \frac{k}{p} - \frac{N - k}{1 - p} = 0 \implies \frac{k}{p} = \frac{N - k}{1 - p} \]
\[ k(1 - p) = p(N - k) \implies k - kp = Np - kp \implies Np = k \implies \hat{p}_{\text{MLE}} = \frac{k}{N} \].
Checking second derivative: \( \frac{d^2\ell}{dp^2} = -\frac{k}{p^2} - \frac{N-k}{(1-p)^2} < 0 \), confirming a maximum.
Answer: \( \hat{p}_{\text{MLE}} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N x_i \).

label.en: Worked Example B — Probability Distributions & Maximum Likelihood (MLE) (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول B — التوزيعات الاحتمالية وتقدير الاحتمال الأقصى (MLE) (تطبيق Medium)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): In training a language model token predictor, a binary token occurs \( k = 3 \) times across \( n = 10 \) independent trials. What is the Maximum Likelihood Estimate \( \hat{p}_{\text{MLE}} \) of the token probability?

Step-by-Step Solution: For a Bernoulli likelihood \( L(p) = p^k (1-p)^{n-k} \), the log-likelihood is \( \ln L = k\ln p + (n-k)\ln(1-p) \). Setting derivative to zero: \( \frac{k}{p} - \frac{n-k}{1-p} = 0 \implies \hat{p} = \frac{k}{n} = \frac{3}{10} = 0.300 \). Final Answer: \( \hat{p}_{\text{MLE}} = 0.300 \).

الحل خطوة بخطوة: For a Bernoulli likelihood \( L(p) = p^k (1-p)^{n-k} \), the log-likelihood is \( \ln L = k\ln p + (n-k)\ln(1-p) \). body.en:
Problem (Hard): Principal Component Analysis on covariance matrix \( \Sigma_{C} \) yields eigenvalues \( \lambda_1 = 63 \) and \( \lambda_2 = 37 \). Determine the percentage of variance \( E_{p} \) explained by the first principal component.

Step-by-Step Solution: The percentage explained is \( \frac{63}{63+37} \times 100\% = 63\% \).

Problem (Easy): A binary classifier \( E(p) \) produces the confusion matrix below with \( \text{TP} = 24 \), \( \text{FP} = 36 \), \( \text{FN} = 21 \), and \( \text{TN} = 60 \). Determine the total number of correct classifications \( L = \text{TP} + \text{TN} \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Summing \( \text{TP} + \text{TN} = 24 + 60 = 84 \).

solution.en: The log-likelihood \( \ln L(\mu) = -\frac{n}{2}\ln(2\pi\sigma^2) - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum (x_i - \mu)^2 \). Setting \( \frac{\partial \ln L}{\partial \mu} = 0 \) yields the sample mean \( \hat{\mu} = \frac{1}{n}\sum x_i = \frac{12}{4} = 3 \). Answer: \( \hat{\mu}_{\text{MLE}} = 3 \).
